title: Sign of the Product of an Array
description:
Define a function `signFunc(x)` that returns:
- `1` if `x` is positive,
- `-1` if `x` is negative,
- `0` if `x` is equal to `0`.

You are given an integer array `nums`. Let `product` be the product of all values in `nums`. Return `signFunc(product)`. Note that multiplying all elements directly can overflow standard 32-bit and 64-bit integer types.
hints: You never need to compute the actual magnitude of the product — only its sign matters.
If any element is 0, the entire product is 0, so you can return 0 immediately.
Start with sign = 1 and negate it every time you encounter a negative number.

examples.explanation: There are 4 negative numbers (even) and no zeros, so the product 144 is positive and we return 1.
The array contains 0, so the product is 0 and we return 0.
There are 3 negative numbers (odd) and no zeros, so the product -1 is negative and we return -1.
